summary: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (~1919–1928). He held posts at the University of Lviv (~1934–1944), Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (~1945–1969), and the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

Eugène Burnouf was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A pupil of Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (~1822–1832), he served at the Collège de France (1832–1852) and the Imprimerie Nationale (~1832–1852).
Eugène Jacquet was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat (~1828–1832) and Eugène Burnouf (~1832–1838).

Eugène Tisserant worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at the Lycee Notre-Dame Saint-Sigisbert, École du Louvre (~1904–1906), and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1904–1907).

Eun Hino is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~2006–2008). He held positions at the University of Tokyo (~2011–2014) and Musashino University (~2014–2018; ~2018).
Eun Maeda was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He served as president (学長) of Toyo University and Ryukoku University.

Eun-su Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini (attested 1997). She taught at the University of Michigan (until 2004) and Seoul National University (from 2004).
Eun-young Choi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Korea University. She held an HK professor post at Geumgang University, attested between 2013 and 2015.

Eva K. Neumaier is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Khenpo Rigzin. She held appointments at the University of Calgary (attested 1992, 2006) and the University of Alberta (attested 2006).

Eva Tichy is a linguist and Indologist who earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1974–1981) and completed her habilitation at the University of Marburg (~1982–1989). She held a chair at the University of Freiburg (1993–2017).

Eva Wilden is an Indologist who completed her MA, Promotion, and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1986–2004). She served as Maître de conférences at the EFEO (2003) and became a professor at the University of Hamburg in 2017.

Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied at Amherst under Robert Thurman and at the University of Toronto under Francisco Varela. His main posts include York University (2002–2005), University of Toronto (~2005–2013), and University of British Columbia (from 2013).

Eviatar Shulman is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1998–2008). He became chairman of the Department of Comparative Religion there in 2009.

Eyal Aviv works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello, Parimal G. Patil, and Michael Puett (attested 2008), and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leiden and Utrecht under Uhlenbeck, van Wijk, and Caland. He served as professor of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1939–1972) and director of the Kern Institute (~1946–1977).
Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a dissertation at the University of Calgary (attested 2001) under Leslie S. Kawamura, A. W. Barber, and X. Jie Yang.
Fa Yao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 1995). He is attested as a visiting lecturer of Theravada Buddhism at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history. She earned her PhD under Pierre-Étienne Will at the EHESS (~1994–1999) and was appointed Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~2001).

Fabio Rambelli works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, having studied under Massimo Raveri and Adriana Boscaro across Venice, Tokyo, and Naples. He held posts at Sapporo University (2001–2002) and UC Santa Barbara (from ~2009).

Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" (1969–2004). She held posts at the University of Florence (~2000) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".
